_comment: SonarQube quality gate as data. Apply it with ./l2-apply-quality-gate.sh (it reads this file).
_usage: Create the gate:        POST /api/qualitygates/create            name=<gate name>
Add one condition:      POST /api/qualitygates/create_condition  gateName=<gate name> metric=<key> op=<GT|LT> error=<threshold>
Make it the default:    POST /api/qualitygates/set_as_default    name=<gate name>
Assign to one project:  POST /api/qualitygates/select            gateName=<gate name> projectKey=<project>
Parameter names changed: create_condition takes gateName (was gateId) and set_as_default takes name (was id).
Authenticate with an admin token as the basic-auth user: curl -u "$SONAR_TOKEN:" ...
Metric keys below are the classic ones; SonarQube 26.x defaults to Multi-Quality-rule mode and maps them (new_blocker_violations -> new_software_quality_blocker_issues) so both spellings work.

conditions._desc: Fail if any new BLOCKER severity issues introduced
Fail if any new CRITICAL severity issues introduced
Fail if new code coverage drops below 80%
Fail if new code duplication exceeds 3%
Fail if any new security hotspots are unreviewed
Fail if security rating on new code is worse than A (1=A, 2=B, 3=C, 4=D, 5=E)
Fail if reliability rating on new code is worse than A
Fail if maintainability rating on new code is worse than A
Fail if new technical debt ratio exceeds 5%

sonarProjectProperties._desc: Add these to sonar-project.properties or sonar-scanner CLI args
